results.name: mwaskom__seaborn-2848
results.summary: pairplot with a partial hue_order fails because PairGrid keeps all rows (hue_vals = data[hue]) while the palette lookup_table is built only from the hue_order levels (categorical_order(data[hue], hue_order)). When an unlisted hue value (e.g. 'virginica') is looked up, HueMapping._lookup_single misses the lookup_table, then calls self.norm(key) (norm is None for categorical mappings), catches the TypeError, and evaluates np.isnan(key) on a string, raising the reported "ufunc 'isnan' not supported" TypeError. The fix should (a) make the isnan fallback in _lookup_single only run for numeric/nan-able keys (or handle non-mapped keys gracefully), and/or (b) filter PairGrid's data/hue_vals to rows whose hue value is in hue_order before mapping, matching old semantics. results.name: psf__requests-2317
results.summary: The bug is caused by `method = builtin_str(method)` in Session.request at requests/sessions.py:428. On Python 3, builtin_str is `str`, so a bytes method b'GET' becomes the literal string "b'GET'" instead of being decoded. The fix is to replace that conversion with decoding of bytes using the already-imported `to_native_string` helper (or an explicit bytes->str decode), preserving str input behavior and remaining a no-op on Python 2. PreparedRequest.prepare_method in models.py only upper/lowercases the already-native string, so no change is needed there. A regression test should be added to test_requests.py asserting a bytes method like b'GET' yields PreparedRequest.method == 'GET'.

results.name: psf__requests-3362
results.summary: Root cause of the confusion: `Response.iter_content(decode_unicode=True)` only performs decoding when `Response.encoding` is set (from the Content-Type header). If `encoding` is None, `stream_decode_response_unicode` yields the raw bytes unchanged. In contrast, `Response.text` falls back to `apparent_encoding` (chardet-based guessing on the already-read full body) when `encoding` is None, which is why it returns unicode. So for an `application/json` response without a charset, `.text` uses chardet while `iter_content(decode_unicode=True)` does not — hence bytes. This is intended design (streaming cannot chardet-guess incrementally), so the appropriate change is to clarify the docstring/docs rather than alter decoding logic. Recommended changes: (1) update the `Response.iter_content` docstring to state decode_unicode only decodes when `encoding` is set and may still yield bytes otherwise; (2) update `Response.text` docstring to note the apparent_encoding fallback differs from iter_content; (3) update `requests/utils.stream_decode_response_unicode` docstring to document the pass-through when `r.encoding is None`; (4) add quickstart docs note; (5) optionally strengthen the existing test `test_response_decode_unicode` to cover the encoding=None case.

results.name: psf__requests-1963
results.summary: The bug is localized to SessionRedirectMixin.resolve_redirects in requests/sessions.py. At line 91 the loop does `prepared_request = req.copy()`, always seeding each redirect hop from the original request, so the effective method set on earlier hops (e.g. 303 turning POST into GET at lines 124-126) is discarded and re-derived from req.method. This causes a later 307 to incorrectly reissue the original POST instead of carrying forward GET. The fix should carry the previous hop's prepared request forward (seeding the first iteration with the original req) and derive the method from the carried-forward request; method-selection heuristics (303/302 not-HEAD -> GET at lines 124-136, 307/308 preserve via the check at lines 141-145) then operate on the effective method. A regression test should be added alongside existing redirect tests in test_requests.py (redirect tests around lines 116-210).

results.name: scikit-learn__scikit-learn-15535
results.summary: In sklearn/metrics/cluster/_supervised.py, check_clusterings() calls check_array() without a dtype argument, so its default dtype='numeric' attempts to convert object-dtype string labels to float, raising "could not convert string to float: 'b'". Add regression tests in sklearn/neighbors/tests/test_neighbors.py for float n_neighbors in the constructor and in kneighbors/radius_neighbors/kneighbors_graph, plus a positive int case, and document the change in the current dev changelog under doc/whats_new/.

results.name: scikit-learn__scikit-learn-10508
results.summary: LabelEncoder.transform (sklearn/preprocessing/label.py lines 115-135) passes y straight to np.searchsorted(self.classes_, y). For an empty list, column_or_1d produces a float64 array; when classes_ is a string dtype (e.g. fit(['a','b'])), numpy refuses the unsafe float64-to-<U32 cast and raises TypeError. With numeric classes_ the cast is fine, hence the inconsistency. Fix: add an early guard after column_or_1d (or before searchsorted) so empty input returns an empty integer array, e.g. if y.size == 0: return np.array([], dtype=np.intp), preserving the integer index dtype of valid transform outputs and leaving non-empty behavior and inverse_transform untouched. A regression test should be added to sklearn/preprocessing/tests/test_label.py.

results.name: sphinx-doc__sphinx-7686
results.summary: The module branch of generate_autosummary_content in sphinx/ext/autosummary/generate.py populates the template variable ns['members'] with the unfiltered dir(obj) (line 249). results.name: matplotlib__matplotlib-25442
results.summary: The AttributeError comes from DraggableBase's callback teardown: when an artist (annotation/offsetbox/legend) is detached from its figure, `_check_still_parented` detects `ref_artist.figure is None` and calls `disconnect()`, but `disconnect()` resolves `self.canvas`, a property built from `self.ref_artist.figure.canvas`; with `figure is None` this raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'canvas'`. results.name: sympy__sympy-17630
results.summary: BlockMatrix._blockmul computes the product as BlockMatrix(self.blocks*other.blocks). Matrix multiplication of block entries containing ZeroMatrix yields scalar Zero entries (e.g. ZeroMatrix*ZeroMatrix -> Zero), and BlockMatrix.__new__ accepts an already-matrix ImmutableDenseMatrix without re-validating entries, so scalar Zero blocks are stored. On the next multiplication, colblocksizes/rowblocksizes access `.cols`/`.rows` on those scalar Zeros, raising AttributeError. The fix should build the product block-by-block in _blockmul and replace any scalar-zero product block with ZeroMatrix(self.rowblocksizes[i], other.colblocksizes[j]) (using the existing compatibility guard), mirroring the same handling in _blockadd for added scalar zeros; alternatively normalize scalar zeros in BlockMatrix.__new__. Add regression tests for b._blockmul(b)._blockmul(b) and block_collapse(b*b*b).

results.name: sympy__sympy-13895
results.summary: The branch-inequivalent rewrite is produced by `Pow.as_numer_denom` (sympy/core/power.py:1163-1196). For `(-(3*x+1)/12)**x` it computes base.as_numer_denom() -> (n=-(3*x+1), d=12); since `d` is real and positive it returns `Pow(n, x)*Pow(d, -x)`, i.e. `(-3*x-1)**x * 12**(-x)`, without checking that the numerator `n` may be negative. The guard only reasons about the denominator's sign (`d.is_real`, `dnonpos`, and the `dnonpos is None and not int_exp` fallback), not the numerator's, so the split is invalid when `n` can be negative and `exp` is not an integer. simplify() itself reaches this through `expr.as_numer_denom()` (sympy/simplify/simplify.py:613) and the following `could_extract_minus_sign`/signsimp block (lines 619-622), which then converts the `-1` term into the `-12**x/12**x` common-denominator form. The least invasive fix is to extend the `Pow.as_numer_denom` guard so the numerator/denominator split of a Pow only occurs when the exponent is an integer or the numerator (and denominator) can be assumed nonnegative; otherwise return `self, S.One`. Mul.as_numer_denom (sympy/core/mul.py:1037) is the analogous code path and should be checked for the same numerator/denominator sign reasoning.

results.name: django__django-11001
results.summary: The bug is in SQLCompiler.ordering_parts (django/db/models/sql/compiler.py:35): the regex r'(.*)\s(ASC|DESC)(.*)' does not match newlines without DOTALL, so for multiline RawSQL ordering expressions the greedy match collapses to just the final line (e.g. ' else null end') plus direction. get_order_by() at line 356 then builds the dedup key from that fragment, and line 358's `seen` check drops later multiline RawSQL clauses whose trailing lines are identical. The fix is to make the regex span newlines (e.g. add re.MULTILINE | re.DOTALL so group(1) captures the entire ordering expression) at line 35; the dedup logic at lines 356-361 is otherwise correct but should be verified with the new regex. A regression test with multiple multiline RawSQL(...).asc()/.desc() expressions sharing a trailing 'else null end' line should be added to tests/queries/tests.py (near existing order_by tests such as test_order_by_extra at line 2030).

results.name: sympy__sympy-12454
results.summary: Matrix.is_upper (MatrixProperties.is_upper) builds index pairs with `for i in range(1, self.rows) for j in range(i)`, which for tall matrices (rows > cols) produces j >= cols and raises IndexError via extract/a2idx. The fix is to bound the inner loop by the column count, e.g. `for j in range(min(i, self.cols))`, preserving correctness (j < i is the sub-diagonal condition) while never indexing out of range. is_lower already guards with range(self.cols) and needs no change; is_upper_hessenberg delegates to a separate eval method and is unrelated. Regression tests for tall matrices belong in test_is_upper in sympy/matrices/tests/test_matrices.py (and the parallel PropertiesOnlyMatrix test in test_commonmatrix.py).

results.summary: partitions() in sympy/utilities/iterables.py creates one dict `ms`, mutates it across iterations, and yields the same object (yields at lines ~1805/1807 and ~1845/1847). The docstring explicitly documents the reuse caveat (lines ~1741-1754) with the `[p for p in partitions(6, k=2)]` example showing repeated {1: 6}, and advises callers to copy. Fix: yield a fresh copy of ms each iteration (both `size=True` tuples and plain dicts), and remove/rewrite the caveat section and the now-stale doctest. Update test_iterables.test_partitions, which currently relies on `.copy()` and the shared-dict behavior, to assert list(partitions(...)) gives independent dicts that aren't mutated on later iterations, and update the docs example in doc/src/modules/utilities/iterables.rst that uses `p.copy()`. Other callers (nT, combinatorics tests) only read size/counts, so no behavioral breakage expected.
